correctness.rationale: Writing elements as a+bε, multiplication is (a,b)(c,d)=(ac,ad+bσ(c)); units are exactly those with nonzero residue and the radical is square-zero. Direct multiplication with an inverse gives the stated inner action. When σ(a)≠a the translating d can reach every second coefficient, so each such a gives one orbit of size q. When σ(a)=a, the multiplier subgroup is the image of c↦c/σ(c), of size (q−1)/(q₀−1), acting freely on nonzero coefficients and fixing zero. This gives the stated distribution, with singleton rows combined in the identity case; q+q₀²−q₀ is strictly increasing in q₀. The action on the radical bimodule forces τρ=ρσ for an isomorphism inducing residue-field automorphism ρ, hence σ=τ because the Galois group is abelian. The map (a,b)↦(a,σ⁻¹(b)) reverses products into the inverse twist, proving the anti-isomorphism criterion. All nonzero zero divisors lie in the radical and all their products vanish. The commutation equation has q² solutions in (b,d) when both residues are fixed, and q otherwise, including the identity twist as probability 1. Exponents 1 and 2 mod 5 have fixed field F₂, are unequal, and are not negatives. New exact enumeration by direct stabilizer tests in /workspace/reproductions/34_pairs_and_rings.py independently reproduced {1:2,31:2,32:30} and 36,736 commuting ordered pairs for each F₃₂ twist and 1024 singleton orbits for the identity. Frozen VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were read, not run.
